checks.left_summary: Core BTC, ETH, and SOL contract specifications use base-asset amount steps.
checks.right_summary: Protocol positions use base quantums convertible to full underlying units.

checks.left_summary: Position P&L is the base position times the USD exit-to-entry price difference.
checks.right_summary: The protocol definition models base positions against quote quantums without inverse or quanto treatment.

checks.left_summary: Realized P&L and total account value are denominated in USDC for the selected perpetual account.
checks.right_summary: Margin caps and quote accounting are denominated in USDC.

checks.left_summary: The index combines Chainlink, Stork, and Pyth oracle inputs.
checks.right_summary: Validator-consensus oracle prices feed collateral, margin, liquidations, and funding.

checks.left_summary: A composite fair mark combines impact and external price components for P&L and margin.
checks.right_summary: The documented oracle drives collateral and liquidation while liquidity tiers scale margin.

checks.left_summary: The engine cancels orders, attempts protected IOC closes, and can transfer positions to LLP.
checks.right_summary: Protocol-generated liquidation orders match resting order-book liquidity with governance-controlled rules.

checks.left_summary: ADL uses opposite positions when LLP cannot cover a bankrupt account and ranks counterparties by leverage and unrealized P&L.
checks.right_summary: Randomly chosen offsetting positions can be deleveraged when an account becomes negative.

checks.left_summary: Selected deployed markets have a one-hour funding period.
The formula samples impact premiums and applies interest and two clamps before dividing by eight.
checks.right_summary: The formula uses proposer-voted premiums and governance-adjustable sampling and clamp parameters.

checks.left_summary: The documented big clamp is converted to a per-hour rate by the funding formula.
checks.right_summary: The cap depends on governance-controlled initial and maintenance margin parameters.

checks.left_summary: Core steps and margins are documented, and sequence continuity is observable, but parameters and executable depth require point-in-time capture.
checks.right_summary: Governance-controlled liquidity tiers and account rate limits require point-in-time capture.

checks.left_summary: Standard and Premium account types trade fee against enforced maker, taker, and cancellation latency.
checks.right_summary: Maker-taker fees are tiered and governance-adjustable, so effective costs require current account state.

checks.left_summary: The protocol runs on an Ethereum Layer 2 and retains operator API, oracle, USDC, and LLP dependencies.
checks.right_summary: dYdX Chain has separate consensus but retains oracle, USDC, validator, and interface dependencies.

checks.left_summary: Official terms impose location, sanctions, wallet-ownership, API-use, and discretionary access restrictions requiring independent review.
checks.right_summary: The operated frontend restricts certain jurisdictions and can enforce close-only or blocked access, requiring independent review.
